chapter_theme: A man who lets his wife's will or his desire for her govern him loses virtue, wealth, standing and even pleasure. The chapter treats household subordination as a failure of his own agency and of his duties to others, and it speaks throughout from the husband's side.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter by fault: desiring the wife (901-902), fearing her (903-906), obeying her (907-909), and a negative summary of all three (910). Kalaignar repeatedly rewrites the chapter so that its target is a bad or arrogant wife, or a man besotted with beauty, not wives as such.

901.reading: Men who fix their desire on the wife do not reach the fine fruit of life, and this same desire is what men intent on action refuse to want.
901.nuance: The verse says only மனை, 'home', and மாண்பயன், 'fine fruit', without naming either. Parimelazhagar supplies virtue as the fruit and wealth-making as the action, so the claim that the household's own goal is lost is partly his construction.

902.reading: The prosperity of one who desires his woman without caring for something else brings him shame, and a great shame in the world besides.
902.nuance: பேணாது has no object in the verse, so what is being neglected is exactly what the commentators must decide.

positions.position: What he abandons is his manliness, and his wealth shames all men because she controls its use.
positions.quote: தன் ஆண்மையை விட்டு மனையாளது பெண்மையை விழைவான்

positions.position: What he fails to tend is virtue and wealth, with no appeal to manliness.
positions.quote: அறத்தினையும் பொருளினையும் பேணாது மனையாளைக் காதலிப் பானது செல்வம்

positions.position: What he neglects is the principle he adopted, as he trails after a woman.

903.reading: The unnatural condition of stooping before one's wife brings a man shame among good people at all times.
903.nuance: The shame is social and comparative. It arises among நல்லார், not in the house.

positions.position: The fault is a husband's fear of any wife: fear is natural to her, so in him it is unnatural and leaves her uncontrolled.
positions.quote: அவள் தான் அஞ்சி ஒழுகுதல் இயல்பாகலின், அவளை அஞ்சுதல் இயல்பின்மையாயிற்று.

positions.position: The fault is yielding to a wife of bad character instead of trying to correct her.

904.reading: A man who fears his wife and has no share in the other life gets no distinction from his capacity for action.

positions.position: மறுமை is the next world, whose fruit he forfeits because he cannot perform household virtue.
positions.quote: தன் மனையாளை அஞ்சி ஒழுகுகின்ற மறுமைப்பயன் இல்லாதானுக்கு

positions.position: The man fears running a family and misses the fruit of the new life that marriage opens; no next world is involved.

905.reading: One who fears his wife will always be afraid to do good to good people.
905.nuance: The harm named is the loss of generosity to outsiders, so fear in the house is treated as a public failure of giving.

positions.position: He fears giving to guests, ascetics and elders, even out of wealth he earned himself.
positions.quote: தான் தேடிய பொருளே யாயினும் அதனால் நல்லார்க்கு நல்லன செய்தலை

positions.position: He reverses the sense: a man anxious to do good without error heeds the wife who watches for error.

906.reading: Even if they live like the gods, those who fear the bamboo-like shoulders of their wives have no worth.
906.nuance: The bamboo epithet is usually praise, but here it makes the fear ridiculous: Parimelazhagar takes it to show how slight the object of terror is, and contrasts it with warriors' shoulders. Kalaignar again limits the verse, to a wife lacking wisdom and character.

907.reading: A woman who has shame holds more greatness than the manhood of one who goes about doing a woman's bidding.
907.nuance: The verse uses gender as a rank and then overturns it: நாண் outranks manhood. Its force still depends on the assumption that being below a woman is a disgrace, so it cuts both ways.

908.reading: Those who act as the woman of the fine brow wishes neither meet their friends' needs nor do good.
908.nuance: Parimelazhagar's reason is practical: she can neither issue the needed orders on her own nor hand over the wealth, so the household's decision-making stalls.

909.reading: Deeds of virtue, ample wealth and the other pursuits are absent in those who do a woman's bidding.
909.nuance: பிறவினை is left open. Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar take it as pleasure, which gives the verse its sting: the man who surrenders for the sake of pleasure ends up losing pleasure too.

910.reading: Those whose minds hold deliberation and who have strength of heart will never have the foolishness that comes of attachment to a woman.
910.nuance: The positive turns the chapter into a claim about mind, not women: the fault is called பேதைமை and is the man's own. Commentators split on இடன், which Parimelazhagar takes as wealth in kings and Manakkudavar as breadth of mind, while Kalaignar hears firmness of heart.

links.note: Both set a wife's or beloved's shoulders against heaven. 906 says that fearing those shoulders leaves no worth even in a godlike life, and 1103 asks whether the lotus-eyed god's world is sweeter than sleep on them. Fear and love differ, but the books value the same intimacy in opposite ways.

Both redefine manliness away from dominance over others. 148 gives பேராண்மை to the man who doesn't look at another's wife, and 907 finds the opposite failure in a man who takes a woman's orders: in each case ஆண்மை is measured by self-command.
428 calls fearing what should be feared the act of the wise. 905 shows the matching error: the fear here lands on doing good, which ought not be feared.

909 says the man who serves a woman's will loses pleasure with everything else. 1107 compares a beloved's embrace to eating one's own share in one's own home, which suggests that the pleasure 909 says is lost belongs to someone still his own master.

source_issues: 903: no Manakkudavar commentary is aligned to this verse.
901-902: Pope's gloss says 'lust after' and 'feminine nature', which are stronger than மனைவிழைவார் and பெண்விழைவான்; these come from Parimelazhagar's framing.
